title: Cached authorization decision served after token revocation
vulnerable_behaviour: The RS caches an active=true introspection result for 300 s and serves the protected resource from the cache after the token was revoked at the IdP.
fixed_behaviour: cache_ttl = 0: every request is introspected, so revocation takes effect on the next request.
termination_trigger: explicit token revocation: POST IdP /revoke token_type_hint=access_token (200)
declared_expected_scope: the revoked access token at every resource server
protected_operation: GET RS /api/data with the revoked Bearer access token
cwe_rule_path: => explicit-termination failure: a downstream verifier retains a pre-termination authorization decision

neighbour_rules.CWE-613 original sense (time-only expira: partially overlapping: the residual window is bounded by the cache TTL (300 s), i.e. a time-limited residual after an explicit trigger

uncertainty.reason: the residual capability is time-bounded by the cache TTL, so classification depends on whether a bounded stale window counts as an explicit-termination failure; the trace records decision_source to make the cache path explicit

lifecycle_event: explicit token revocation: POST IdP /revoke token_type_hint=access_token (200)
normative_basis: Declared laboratory cache-invalidation policy; RFC 7662 permits bounded caching, so the fixture tests its stated post-revocation contract rather than a universal zero-delay rule.
